items.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: He’s been a great influence... he was always to me always trying to deal with the pinnacle of the music... he meant a lot to me in terms of my development

ctx.x: And I was listening to it and I said I think Hubert Laws listened to you.

Oh no, no I listened to him. Oh no, no, no, no. He’s been a great influence because obviously he had the training in Juilliard and Julius Baker and all that stuff and he is an interesting person because he always explored pop music, jazz music, Latin music, classical music. And he was a great influence because he, in a way, his music always reflected to me interesting dichotomies. Because you take a CD that he did entitled “Morning Star,” Rogers Grant, great composition. I mean a beautiful arrangements by Don…
I’m trying to remember the name of the record , “Sunflower”?
